previous.note: Occurred. First qualifying docket entry: the FTC-referred stipulated order against Cerebral, Inc. (permanent injunction, $5.1M consumer redress, $10M civil penalty with $2M payable) over its data-disclosure and cancellation business practices, filed by DOJ in U.S. v. Cerebral, Inc., No. 1:24-cv-21376 (S.D. Fla.), Document 6 entered on the docket 2024-04-15 (complaint filed 2024-04-12; the FTC copy shows the judge's signature block blank, so court entry came later). The criterion counts a filed settlement over 'prescribing or business practices'. The prescribing-specific outcome came later: the EDNY non-prosecution agreement dated 2024-11-01 ($3.652M forfeiture, $2.922M deferred penalty; announced 2024-11-04) for Controlled Substances Act conduct in 2019-2022. The 2022 N.D. Iowa qui tam (1:22-cv-00055) was declined by the US and voluntarily dismissed on 2023-11-06, so it does not count.

evidence.title: Frontline Clinician Psilocybin Study (NCT05163496), University of Washington, Phase 3, actual start 2022-03-03
ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 search: studies of psilocybin registered as Phase 3, sorted by start date (16 records)
Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of COMP360 in Participants With TRD (COMP005, NCT05624268), Phase 3, actual start 2023-01-24

previous.note: Criterion (b): the actual start date recorded on CT.gov for a trial registered as Phase 3 whose product is psilocybin, any sponsor, any indication; the readings say any Phase 3 psilocybin trial counts. A CT.gov search of Phase 3 psilocybin studies sorted by start date returns NCT05163496 first: University of Washington, 'Frontline Clinician Psilocybin Study', registered PHASE3, psilocybin 25 mg (Usona Institute) vs niacin, n=30, actual start 2022-03-03, completed, results posted. Applied as written: true on 2022-03-03. Flag for recheck: this is a small investigator-initiated trial. The first industry-run Phase 3 is Compass COMP005 (NCT05624268, first posted 2022-11-22, actual start 2023-01-24), then COMP006 (2023-02-14) and Usona uAspire (2024-03-13). If the registry means sponsor-run registrational trials only, the date is 2023-01-24; the state is occurred either way.

previous.note: First qualifying filing found: the securities class action Kachrodia v. Acadia Healthcare Company, Inc., M.D. Tenn. No. 3:24-cv-01238, docketed 2024-10-16 (amended 2024-10-21; Dyar followed 2024-10-29; consolidated complaint 2025-07-10; motion to dismiss denied 2026-07-24). The complaint alleges that Acadia detained 'patients against their will, even when such detention was not medically necessary' and misled investors about it, the conduct described in the NYT investigation, so a shareholder class action counts under the criterion. Acadia first disclosed it in the 10-Q filed 2024-10-30. The only earlier post-2024-09-04 federal suit naming Acadia in RECAP (Jenkins, W.D. Tenn., 2024-09-18) is an overtime case. State-court patient suits filed between 2024-09-04 and 2024-10-16 could not be excluded (no state docket search), so the date could move earlier if one surfaces.

evidence.publisher: U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Wisconsin (via CourtListener RECAP)

previous.note: Applied as written. H.N. v. Anthem BCBS, Marsh & McLennan Companies, Inc. and the Marsh McLennan Plan (D. Mass. 1:26-cv-11454, complaint docketed 2026-03-26) is brought by a plan beneficiary against the claims administrator and the employer that self-funds the plan. Its Second Cause of Action, 'Violation of MHPAEA (Breach of Fiduciary Duty and Claim for Appropriate Equitable Relief under 29 U.S.C. 1132(a)(3)) (ALL DEFENDANTS)', pleads fiduciary breaches by all defendants based on MHPAEA violations in the plan's administration of mental health benefits, so (a) and (b) are met; it is not a suit only under 502(a)(1)(B) against an insurer. Caveats: in substance a benefit-denial suit, not the Schlichter-style class action in the readings; RECAP coverage is partial; a like pleading predates 2026 (W v. Ascension Wisconsin, 2025-09-17). Later alternate: L.P. v. NC Dental Society (2026-04-13).
